Automate repetitive web research into tables
The poster uses Claude Code with Browser Use and Chrome so a browser agent navigates, extracts and structures web data, returning results in a table.
·
Aug 1, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
The source describes a simple setup: connect Claude Code to Browser Use and Chrome, then prompt it with a high-level instruction like using Browser Use to find and organize jobs. From there, the browser agent handles the repetitive steps on its own by navigating sites, collecting the requested information, and returning it in a structured table, while the person mainly defines the task.
How it went
The reported result was successful enough for the author’s own job-research task, with the main benefit being a faster alternative to manually searching, opening pages, copying details, and organizing them. The source does not give detailed prompt variants or setup instructions, so reproducibility is limited.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Use a browser tool to visit [list of websites or search pages] and collect [data fields, e.g. product name, price, rating, link] for [topic or query]. Put the results in a table, save it as a CSV at [file path], and note any pages you could not read or values you were unsure about. Stop once you have covered [number] items or all listed sources, and show me the table.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeWorkflows/comments/1vwtyub/workflow_automating_repetitive_web_research_with
